marks.gloss_en: מתקיף לה: אלא מעתה, חישב להוציא כל ביתו -- הכי נמי דלא מיחייב עד דמפיק לכוליה?! -- if a person's purpose sets the measure, one who planned to carry out his whole house would not be liable until he carried all of it
התם בטלה דעתו אצל כל אדם -- there his intention is void against that of all people (= p_kol_beito_batla_daato)
R' Meir held liable even one who carries out a single wheat seed for sowing
Abaye: whoever acts [with something], acts on his first intention -- so the forgotten storing purpose is not nullified

דתניא: ... ובא אחר והוציאו נתחייב זה במחשבתו של זה -- the baraita makes another liable by the storer's thought, which the mishna's 'only at its measure' does not (kind svara: no kind names a bare דתניא)
the mishna: and any [other] person is liable for it only at its measure
Rav Nachman: one who carried out a dried-fig bulk for eating and reconsidered it for sowing, or for sowing and reconsidered it for eating, is liable
Rava's dilemma: one carried out half a dried fig for sowing, it swelled, and he reconsidered it for eating -- is he liable?
Rava: and if you say [in the first dilemma that he is liable] -- one carried out a dried-fig bulk for eating, it shrank, and he reconsidered it for sowing -- is he liable?
תניתוה: Abba Shaul gives the loaves a fig measure. [stam:] ואמאי? לימא: מדלענין יוצא בכזית, לענין שבת נמי בכזית! -- a measure significant for another law (yotze) does not set the Shabbat measure
Rava's question: one threw an olive-bulk of teruma into an impure house -- since it joins [an egg-bulk of food] for impurity, is he liable for Shabbat too?
